title: How to mute yourself in Zoom on Mac: step by step for Zoom Workplace
metaTitle: How to Mute Yourself in Zoom on Mac (Shortcut and Menu)
description: Learn how to mute yourself in Zoom on Mac with Command+Shift+A, the Audio button, and hold Space to talk. Steps for Zoom Workplace.

intro: To mute yourself in Zoom on Mac, press Command+Shift+A during a meeting, or click the Audio icon in the meeting controls toolbar. A red diagonal line across the microphone means you are muted, and the line goes away when you unmute.
tldr: Press Command+Shift+A during a meeting to mute, and press it again to unmute.
Or click the Audio icon in the meeting toolbar. A red diagonal line means you are muted.
Hold the Space bar to talk for a moment without unmuting for the whole call.
Turn on Keep my microphone muted in Settings > Meetings & webinars if you often join with sound on.

blocks.text: The fastest fix: Command+Shift+A

Zoom's own hot-key article gives one shortcut for muting audio on a Mac. Press Command+Shift+A once to mute. Press it again to unmute. You do not need to open a menu or find a button. Your hands stay on the keyboard, which matters when you are presenting or typing notes during a call. Learn this one first, then add the others.

Some tips online list Option+A or Command+Control+A. Zoom's Mac hot-key article documents neither one. If a shortcut does nothing, do not guess a new one. Check your keyboard shortcut settings first, as described later in this guide, and confirm the meeting window is the active window.

blocks.caption: Mute controls on a Mac, as Zoom documents them

blocks.text: Mute with the Audio icon in the toolbar

Move your pointer over the Zoom window during the meeting. The meeting controls toolbar shows the Audio icon, which looks like a microphone. Click it to mute. When you are muted, a red diagonal line crosses the microphone. Click again and the line disappears. That line is your main signal, so check it before you speak.

The label changes between sources. Zoom's muting article calls the control Audio. Zoom's troubleshooting page refers to a Mute button with an upward arrow beside it, and that arrow opens the list of microphones. Read the toolbar for whichever label matches your version. If you cannot find it, check the More menu first.

Zoom redesigned the desktop app in December 2025 with version 6.7. The in-meeting toolbar shows fewer buttons now, and others sit in a More menu. Spring 2026 changes began rolling out on March 23, 2026 with the 7.0.0 client upgrade. If your toolbar looks different from older guides, look in More before you assume the control is missing.
Hold Space to talk without unmuting

Zoom describes this as temporary unmuting. Hold the Space bar, speak, and let go. You are muted again as soon as you release the key. This suits a quick answer during someone else's presentation, or a short comment you do not want to leave running. It does not suit a long speech.

Holding Space has one limit. It works only if the host has not stopped you from unmuting. If the host blocks unmuting, holding Space does nothing, and you cannot unmute yourself at all. Zoom's muting article covers this case. If you need to talk and the setting is locked, ask the host to allow it.
Stay muted from the moment you join

Many people join with sound on by habit, then scramble to mute while the meeting is already running. You can change this once. Open Zoom Workplace, click your profile picture, and choose Settings. Select Meetings & webinars. Under When joining meetings and webinars, turn on Keep my microphone muted.

For one meeting only, skip the setting. On the join screen, tick Don't connect to audio before you click Join. Zoom's join-muted article covers the desktop app on Windows and macOS, and the mobile app. It does not cover the Zoom Web App, so a browser meeting may behave differently.
Change the shortcut if Command+Shift+A clashes

Another app may already use Command+Shift+A. In that case, rebind the Zoom shortcut. Open profile picture > Settings, click the Keyboard shortcuts icon, click the shortcut, then press the new key combination. Zoom notes that some shortcuts can be global, which means they work when Zoom is not the active window. Some options need the latest app version.

Choose a combination that no other app uses. Avoid keys you already use for browser tabs or system tools. Test the new keys during a call with a colleague who can tell you whether you were heard. Keep the new shortcut on a sticky note for the first week, because muscle memory takes time.
Check microphone permission before you blame Zoom

If the mute icon changes but nobody hears you, macOS may be blocking Zoom from using the microphone. Open Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security. Under Privacy, click Microphone, then turn on the toggle for Zoom. If Zoom is already running, it prompts you to restart. Zoom says a full Mac restart is not needed.

Browser meetings use different permissions. Zoom's Web App article says the browser needs microphone access in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone. Tick the box for Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge. When the browser prompts you after you click New Meeting, click Allow. Zoom lists Chrome 102 or higher and Safari 16.4 or higher for the Web App.
Which Zoom version you need on a Mac

Zoom's release notes list 7.2.5 (90525) as the latest macOS desktop build. It was released October 31, 2026. The notes call the macOS app Zoom Workplace. Zoom's system requirements page lists macOS 10.15 Catalina or later for the desktop app.

Zoom's minimum-version page says users below its minimum must update before they can sign in or join the desktop app. They can join through the web app instead. Update before an important call, not during it. Zoom's permissions guide lists macOS 10.14 Mojave, which conflicts with the 10.15 requirement, so check the requirements page when in doubt.
Mistakes people make on calls

The most common mistake is talking while muted. Preply surveyed 1,360 Americans in February 2024. About 55% said they tried to speak on a work video call, found they were on mute, and gave up on what they were going to say. The survey is self-reported, and Preply is a language-learning company, so read the number as a signal, not a measured rate.

The second mistake is trusting memory over the icon. Check the red line before a sentence, especially after you switch speakers or share your screen. The third is joining with sound on by default. One settings change stops the unmute scramble at the start of every call.

The fourth mistake is copying an old shortcut from a forum. Option+A appears in some older tips, but Zoom's Mac article does not document it. Use Command+Shift+A, which Zoom does document, and test it before a meeting that matters.
What to do next

Once muting feels automatic, look at the next problem on your list. If your screen looks black when you present, read [how to fix a black screen share in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/fix-a-black-screen-share-in-zoom). If you want a copy of the call for later, read [how to record a Zoom meeting on Mac](/how-to/record-a-meeting-in-zoom).
Set one shortcut and one join setting today. Then your next call starts quietly, and your attention stays on the conversation instead of the microphone.

faq.question: Is Option+A the Zoom mute shortcut on Mac?
faq.answer: Not according to Zoom's Mac hot-key article. Zoom documents Command+Shift+A for muting and unmuting audio on macOS. If Option+A works for you, someone probably changed it in Keyboard shortcuts settings.

faq.question: How do I know if I am muted in Zoom on Mac?
faq.answer: Look at the Audio icon in the meeting controls toolbar. A red diagonal line across the microphone means you are muted. The line disappears when you unmute, according to Zoom's muting article.

faq.question: Can I mute myself in Zoom on Mac from a browser?
faq.answer: Zoom's muting article covers the desktop app only. Check the controls inside the browser meeting before you rely on a shortcut. Zoom's Web App pages list Chrome 102 or higher and Safari 16.4 or higher.

faq.question: Why is my Zoom mute shortcut not working?
faq.answer: Click inside the meeting window first so it is active, then press the shortcut again. Check Settings > Keyboard shortcuts in case it was changed. If the host has blocked unmuting, the shortcut and push-to-talk both fail.

faq.question: Can I stay muted every time I join a Zoom meeting?
faq.answer: Yes. Open Settings from your profile picture, select Meetings & webinars, and turn on Keep my microphone muted. For one meeting only, tick Don't connect to audio on the join screen before you click Join.

faq.question: What is push-to-talk in Zoom on Mac?
faq.answer: Holding the Space bar unmutes you for as long as you hold it. Release the key and you are muted again. It only works when the host allows you to unmute.

faq.question: Which macOS version does the Zoom desktop app need?
faq.answer: Zoom's system requirements page lists macOS 10.15 Catalina or later. Its macOS permissions guide mentions 10.14 Mojave, so check the requirements page before you upgrade.

faq.question: Is the Zoom app on Mac still called Zoom Client?
faq.answer: Zoom's release notes call the macOS app Zoom Workplace. The latest macOS desktop build listed there is 7.2.5 (90525), released October 31, 2026.

steps.name: Open Zoom Workplace and join your meeting
steps.text: Open the Zoom Workplace app on your Mac. Join or start the meeting as usual. The meeting controls appear once you are in the call. Mute controls only work inside a live meeting.

steps.name: Find the Audio icon in the toolbar
steps.text: Move the pointer over the Zoom window so the meeting controls toolbar is visible. Look for the Audio icon, which is shaped like a microphone. Some builds label the same control Mute.
steps.tip: If you do not see Audio, check the More menu. Zoom moved some toolbar buttons there in its December 2025 redesign.

steps.name: Click Audio to mute
steps.text: Click the Audio icon once. A red diagonal line appears across the microphone. That line tells you that you are muted, so nobody on the call hears you until you unmute.

steps.name: Use the keyboard shortcut instead
steps.text: Press Command+Shift+A while the meeting window is active. Press the same keys to unmute. This is faster than moving the pointer, and it keeps your hands on the keyboard during a presentation.
steps.tip: Click inside the meeting window first if the keys do nothing.

steps.name: Check the mute state before you speak
steps.text: Glance at the microphone icon before you start a sentence. No red line means your mic is live. A red line means the call cannot hear you, even if you are talking.

steps.name: Talk for a moment with push-to-talk
steps.text: Hold the Space bar to unmute briefly. Speak, then release the key to mute again. Push-to-talk stops working if the host has blocked you from unmuting. In that case, ask the host to allow it.
steps.tip: Use this for short replies, not for long speeches.

steps.name: Set mute on join
steps.text: Open Zoom Workplace and click your profile picture. Choose Settings, then select Meetings & webinars. Under When joining meetings and webinars, turn on Keep my microphone muted. Your next meeting starts with your mic off.

steps.name: Change the shortcut if it clashes
steps.text: Click your profile picture, choose Settings, then click the Keyboard shortcuts icon. Click the current shortcut for mute, then press the new key combination. Some shortcuts can work as global shortcuts, even when Zoom is not in focus.
steps.tip: Pick keys that no other app uses, and test them in a quiet call first.

shortcuts.action: Mute or unmute audio in a meeting

troubleshooting.problem: The red line does not change when I press the shortcut
troubleshooting.fix: Click inside the Zoom meeting window so it is active, then press Command+Shift+A again. If nothing changes, check whether the shortcut was rebound in Keyboard shortcuts settings, or whether the host has blocked unmuting.

troubleshooting.problem: Zoom says it does not detect my microphone
troubleshooting.fix: Unplug the microphone and plug it back in. Check that no physical mute switch is on, then raise the Mac's system volume. In Zoom, open profile picture > Settings > Audio and select the microphone under Microphone.

troubleshooting.problem: The mute icon changes, but nobody hears me
troubleshooting.fix: Open Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone, then turn on the toggle for Zoom. If Zoom is already running, it prompts you to restart. Zoom says a Mac restart is not needed.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot unmute at all, even with Space
troubleshooting.fix: The host may have blocked unmuting. Push-to-talk does not work in that case either. Ask the host to allow you to unmute before you try again.
